The Grizzly Hills, located in southeastern Northrend, is a forested area, surrounded by the Howling Fjord to the south, the Dragonblight to the west, and Zul'Drak to the north. It is is the ancestral homeland of the furbolgs, most of whom live in their capital of Grizzlemaw. Both the iron dwarf settlement of Thor Modan and the Ice troll fortress of Drak'Tharon Keep, now occupied by the Scourge, can be found in the north. The hills are home to an independent population of local humans simply called the "trappers", whose signature trading posts can be found throughout the region.
The Venture Co. is also found here, deforesting the land as part of a large-scale operation throughout the region. Many of the local trappers have become part of the mysterious Wolfcult, an army of worgen led by the resurrected Arugal from Bloodmoon Isle. Some furbolgs have also been affected by the corruption of an Old God, being driven to insanity.

Although plagued by [[trappers]] and the deforestation efforts of the [[goblin]] [[Venture Company]], the furbolgs' most imminent threat comes from the north, where [[undead]] [[Drakkari tribe|Drakkari]] [[ice troll]]s have begun pouring from their stronghold of [[Drak'Tharon Keep]].|''[[The Art of World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King]]'', pg. 94}} The '''Grizzly Hills''', located in southeastern [[Northrend]], is a forested area, surrounded by the [[Howling Fjord]] to the south, the [[Dragonblight]] to the west, and [[Zul'Drak]] to the north. It is is the ancestral homeland of the [[furbolg]]s, most of whom live in their capital of [[Grizzlemaw]].[[Wrath of the Lich King Expansion Features/Zones#Grizzly Hills|Wrath of the Lich King Features: Grizzly Hills]] Both the [[iron dwarf]] settlement of [[Thor Modan]] and the [[Ice troll]] [[fortress]] of [[Drak'Tharon Keep]], now occupied by the [[Scourge]], can be found in the north. The hills are home to an independent population of [[Humans of Northrend|local humans]] simply called the "[[trappers]]", whose signature trading posts can be found throughout the region. The [[Venture Co.]] is also found here, deforesting the landhttp://pc.ign.com/articles/814/814776p1.html{{Dead link}} as part of a large-scale operation throughout the region. Many of the local trappers have become part of the mysterious [[Wolfcult]], an army of [[worgen]] led by the resurrected [[Arugal]] from [[Bloodmoon Isle]].http://www.eurogamer.net/article.php?article_id=138018&page=1 Some furbolgs have also been affected by the corruption of an [[Yogg-Saron|Old God]], being driven to insanity.http://www.wowinsider.com/2008/05/09/more-wrath-of-the-lich-king-impressions-and-information-coming-o/{{Dead link}} ==History== {{stub/Lore-section}} [[File:grizzhills.jpg|thumb|left|Grizzly Hills landscape in {{g|wotlk}}.]] The Grizzly Hills are the childhood home of the bear gods [[Ursoc]] and [[Ursol]], who roamed the region as adventurous cubs countless millennia ago before they matured into [[Wild God]]s.[[Tome of the Ancients]]''[[Exploring Azeroth: Northrend]]'', pg. 26 Ursoc ruled over the region, which he roamed with his children [[Orsonn]] and [[Kodian]].[[Children of Ursoc]] In 4,500 [[BDP]], [[saronite]]—the blood of the [[Old God]] [[Yogg-Saron]]—had begun to spread through [[Northrend]]. A group of [[night elf]] [[druid]]s from the [[Cenarion Circle]] led by [[Fandral Staghelm]] cut branches from the [[World Tree]] [[Nordrassil]] and planted them in areas where saronite had spread, creating [[Great Tree]]s across Azeroth. They planted the largest branch above the largest saronite growth in the mountains of Northrend, creating the new World Tree [[Vordrassil|Andrassil]] ("Crown of the Snow"). [[Malfurion Stormrage]] and the rest of the Circle were furious that the branches had been planted without their approval, but the plan initially appeared to work; for decades, Andrassil towered over Northrend, and all seemed well. In time, however, Andrassil's roots came into contact with the [[Prison of Yogg-Saron]]. The Old God corrupted the tree, driving all nearby creatures to madness and triggering sudden violence between Northrend's [[taunka]] and [[forest nymph]]s. The Cenarion Circle had no choice but to destroy Andrassil. They felled the tree and renamed it [[Vordrassil]] ("Broken Crown").{{Ref WoWCV1|124}} The furbolgs of the Grizzly Hills later made their capital, [[Grizzlemaw]], from Vordrassil's trunk.[[Vordrassil's Sapling]] For generations, the furbolg tribes who worshipped Ursoc lived in relative peace, with no conflict with the neighboring [[Drakkari tribe|Drakkari]] [[ice trolls|trolls]], but shortly before the [[war against the Lich King]] they began facing incursions from [[human]] [[trappers]] and the [[goblin]] [[Venture Company]]. The [[Alliance]] and [[Horde]] considered the Grizzly Hills an untamed and forgotten wilderness frontier prior to the war, although the Alliance maintained a minor presence in the region in the form of [[Amberpine Lodge]] for use by their [[woodsmen]] in the area.[[Lieutenant Dumont#Quotes|Lieutenant Dumont quotes]]''[[Exploring Azeroth: Northrend]]'', pg. 30 ===Wrath of the Lich King=== {{Wotlk-section}} During the [[war against the Lich King|war in Northrend]] in 27 [[ADP]], the [[Lich King]] raised [[Arugal|Archmage Arugal]] from the dead in [[Silverpine Forest]],[[Out of Body Experience]] in order to convert the [[human]] [[trappers]] of Grizzly Hills into [[worgen]]. At the head of the [[Wolfcult]], the [[Shade of Arugal]] spread the [[worgen curse]] in [[Silverbrook]] and [[Solstice Village]], then settled in [[Shadowfang Tower]] on the [[Bloodmoon Isle]], where he was ultimately killed by the [[adventurer]]s.''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: The Eastern Kingdoms]]'', pg. 99 When the [[Alliance]] and [[Horde]] forces arrived, they respectively settled in [[Amberpine Lodge]] and [[Conquest Hold]], from where they began to fight over control of [[Venture Bay]] and [[Blue Sky Logging Grounds]].[[Keep Them at Bay]][[Keep Them at Bay!]] ===Exploring Azeroth=== {{Novel-section}} Following the [[war against the Jailer]] in 36 ADP, the [[Bronzebeard]] brothers visited Grizzly Hills, where they discovered that the [[Venture Company]]'s mining and clear-cutting operations had resumed. The [[goblin]]s once again had full control over [[Venture Bay]] as the [[Alliance]]-[[Horde]] conflict over the region ceased.''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: Northrend]]'', pg. 29 They reported that the [[Trappers]] were still active in [[Silverbrook]] and [[Solstice Village]], though they retained their old isolationist personality, while [[Camp Oneqwah]] had greatly expanded on account of the refugees who made the village their new home.''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: Northrend]]'', pg. 34 ==Geography== The Grizzly Hills are located in the eastern reaches of [[Northrend]]. To the north is the ice troll region of [[Zul'Drak]]. South lies the peninsula of the [[Howling Fjord]], and west is the [[Dragonblight]]. The region has low, green foothills laced with pine trees, craggy mountains, and picturesque rivers. ===Maps and subregions=== [[File:VZ-Grizzly Hills.jpg|thumb|left|Map of the Grizzly Hills.]] {| class="darktable hlist" |- | *[[Amberpine Lodge]] *[[Arriga Footbridge]] *[[Ashwood Lake]] *[[Ashwood Post]] *[[Aspen Grove Post]] *[[Blackriver Logging Camp]] *[[Bloodmoon Isle]] **[[Shadowfang Tower]] *[[Blue Sky Logging Grounds]] *[[Bonesnap's Camp]] *[[Boulder Hills]] *[[Broken Bluffs|The Broken Bluffs]] *[[Camp Oneqwah]] *[[Conquest Hold]] **[[Conquest Pit|The Conquest Pit]] *[[Drak'atal Passage]] *[[Drakil'jin Ruins]] *[[Drak'Tharon Keep]] *[[Dun Argol]] *[[Duskhowl Den]] *[[Eastwind Shore]] *[[Evergreen Trading Post]] *[[Forest's Edge Post]] *[[Forgotten Overlook|The Forgotten Overlook]] *[[Frozen Sea|The Frozen Sea]] *[[Granite Springs]] *[[Grizzlemaw]] *[[Harkor's Camp]] *[[Heart's Blood Shrine]] *[[Heartwood Trading Post]] *[[Hollowstone Mine]] *[[Prospector's Point]] *[[Path of Iron|The Path of Iron]] *[[Rage Fang Shrine]] *[[Redwood Trading Post]] *[[Ruins of Drak'Zin]] *[[Ruins of Tethys]] *[[Ruuna's Camp]] *[[Silverbrook Hills]] **[[Silverbrook]] *[[Solstice Village]] *[[Thor Modan]] *[[Ursoc's Den]] *[[Venture Bay]] *[[Voldrune]] **[[Voldrune Dwelling]] *[[Vordrassil Pass]] *[[Vordrassil's Heart]] *[[Vordrassil's Limb]] *[[Vordrassil's Tears]] *[[Westfall Brigade Encampment]] *[[White Pine Trading Post]] *[[Zeb'Halak]] **[[Zim'bo's Hideout]] |- || ---- ;[[Undisplayed location]]s *[[Vordrassil]] |- || ---- ;Removed locations *[[Drak'ural]] *[[Spruce Point Post]] |- || ---- ;[[Lore location]]s *[[North Sea|The North Sea]] |- || ---- ;{{WC3-inline}} [[Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos|Warcraft III]] *[[Frozen Coast]] |} {{clear|left}} ===Instances=== {| class="darktable" ! Access |- | [[Howling Fjord]] || {{Alliance}} {{Horde}} || 58 - 80 | South || By foot, or by flight path |- | [[Dragonblight]] || {{Alliance}} {{Horde}} || 61 - 80 | West || By foot, or by flight path |- | [[Zul'Drak]] || {{Alliance}} {{Horde}} || 64 - 80 | North || By foot, or by flight path |} ==Notable characters== {{main|Grizzly Hills NPCs}} The Grizzly Hills is home to several characters of note. At the [[Westfall Brigade Encampment]], [[Gryan Stoutmantle]] leads the [[Westfall Brigade]] in the fight against the [[Horde]] and surrounding enemies. The Horde is led by [[Conqueror Krenna]] at [[Conquest Hold]] and [[Tormak the Scarred]], chieftain of the local [[taunka]] [[tribe]], at [[Camp Oneqwah]]. Other notable characters include the captive ice troll [[Drakuru]], the famous adventurer [[Harrison Jones]], the hunter of worgen [[Sasha]] and her mysterious archenemy [[Shade of Arugal]], and the furbolg [[deity]] [[Ursoc]], horribly twisted by his [[tainted]] rebirth. ==PvP== [[File:Blue Sky Logging Grounds.jpg|thumb|[[Blue Sky Logging Grounds]]]] There are a number of [[daily quest]]s in the Grizzly Hills that focus on [[PvP]] combat and a general conflict between the [[Alliance]] and Horde to control [[Venture Bay]], [[Blackriver Logging Camp]], and [[Blue Sky Logging Grounds]]. Daily quests include tasks to recover parts and assist [[NPC]]s, as well as killing opposition NPCs and [[player]]s. Players from both [[faction]]s can speak to NPCs at Blue Sky Logging Grounds to ride a log downstream to the bay where additional quests can be found. Venture Bay can be captured by either faction, which spawns defenders and permits access to the bay's [[vendor]]s. ==Quests== {{Main|Grizzly Hills quests}} There are several [[quest chain]]s in the Grizzly Hills. The Alliance starts out at [[Amberpine Lodge]] and are first tasked with taking care of the wildlife and restocking supplies. Players are then ordered to strike up an alliance with the local hunters and trappers based out of [[Silverbrook]], who have a dark secret. Having figured out the situation, players are then sent to figure out what went wrong with [[Vordrassil]], the failed [[World Tree]], and other problems at [[Westfall Brigade Encampment]]. Both sides find their way to [[Granite Springs]] to deal with the [[Scourge]]-infested trolls in the area in quest chains that send players to [[Drak'Tharon Keep]] and to the far eastern side of the *{{RaceIcon|Vrykul|Female}} [[Syreian the Bonecarver]] Other notable creatures: *{{RaceIcon|SpiritBear}} [[Arcturis]] ==In the RPG== {{RPG-section}} '''Grizzly Hills''' can remind you of other forests during wintertime, except that winter here is year-round. The trees are tall and thick, the pine needles and crisp, clean air produce a pleasant scent, the snow leaves the ground clean and fresh, and the hills themselves are high enough for decent elevation but low enough and gradual enough to be easily climbed. It's one of the nicest regions in [[Northrend]]. The [[Dwarf|dwarves]] at [[Thor Modan]] aren't the only residents. [[Furbolg]]s dominate the region, and they make fine neighbors when they're not attacking. The [[Scourge]] has a presence here as well, but not strong enough to do much more than block the northwest corner. Wild animals roam the hills, providing plenty of meat, fur, and entertainment. It's not an easy land by any stretch, but it's handsome and fierce and full of life.''[[Lands of Mystery]]'', pg. 102 As the [[human]] town of [[Valgarde]] grew in [[Howling Fjord]] to the south, its residents forced the Drakkari and the furbolgs back into the Grizzly Hills and beyond, making the region safe enough for farmers to till the land.''[[Lands of Mystery]]'', pg. 106 ===History=== [[File:Grizzly HillsArt.jpg|thumb|Art from ''[[Lands of Mystery]]''.]] The furbolgs claim they were the first people in these hills. So do the [[Drakkari tribe|Drakkari]], though they're concentrated to the north in [[Zul'Drak]]. But actually, they're both wrong. Dwarves were here first. At least that's what [[Hardigan Ironjaw]], of the Thor Modan expedition, tells. He says the [[Titan]]s placed dwarves here, after they'd created them. It was an experiment to see if they could survive on their own. They not only survived but flourished, spreading southward and into what would later become [[Kalimdor]] and the other continents. Hardigan thinks he can find evidence of their ancestors here in the hills, and uncover truths about their race's early culture. The [[Explorers' Guild]] thought it likely enough to send him here, at any rate. [[Brann Bronzebeard]] believes dwarves did start in the north, since the Titans were there, but he's not sure they ever settled up there. Regardless, all this was well before any surviving history. Furbolgs don't keep careful records beyond births, deaths, marriages, blood feuds and hunting tallies. The Drakkari wouldn't have cared about dwarves even if they'd seen them, unless it was how they tasted on a spit. So no one really knows what went on here back then. Other stories say that the Drakkari built [[Drak'Tharon Keep]] before the furbolgs built [[Grizzlemaw]]. Supposedly, the [[Frostpaw tribe|Frost Paws]] gathered the tribes together in part to fend off the new Drakkari threat. Both races were here and hated each other — the furbolgs had the numbers but with their new keep, the Drakkari were more organized, and the trolls were always more unified than the furbolgs. The existence of Grizzlemaw affected the balance, and the furbolgs' victory over the Drakkari in a series of skirmishes may have led to the keep's eventual loss of Drak'Tharon to the Scourge. You definitely want to stay alert in the Grizzly Hills. Furbolgs don't attack unless you trespass on their lands, or threaten their kin, or steal their prey, or look like you could pose a threat later. Drakkari attack on sight, and so do Scourge forces. The dwarves just want to know what you've seen. A dwarven prospector finally uncovered what the Thor Modan expedition was seeking — an ancient relic clearly made by dwarves. The relic is an enormous and heavy statue of iron. The problem is, he found the statue in a cave between Grizzlemaw and Drak'Tharon Keep. The heroes will have to find and retrieve the relic without getting caught by the Scourge or the furbolgs, all the while avoiding the wild beasts in the area.''[[Lands of Mystery]]'', pg. 104 ===People and culture=== This region is the furbolg homeland, and they outnumber every other race here combined. If you've never seen these massive bear-men, that's exactly what they are: enormous creatures with a bear's build and fur and basic features, but a man's hands and, to a limited extent, mind. That's a dangerous combination, and they're powerful in a fight. Fortunately, they're not aggressive beyond their own territory. The dwarves at Thor Modan have run-ins with furbolgs on a regular basis, since furbolgs feel dwarf kinsmen are trespassers and grave-robbers. Furbolgs are surprisingly friendly to travelers, though, and can greet you warmly once you assure them you lay no claim to anything in the hills. Although rumors say they're less approving of large groups, and particularly wary of strange races, but no one can't blame them for their caution. The furbolgs have a city here, Grizzlemaw, but it holds less than half their number. The rest are gathered in clans and scattered throughout the region. Each clan has its own totem, and when you see one you know you've entered [[Snowspring clan|Snowspring]] territory or [[Winterpaw clan|Winterpaw]] land or [[Snow Flurry clan|Snow Flurry]] hunting grounds or any of the others. It's best to declare yourself openly once you see the totem, since a furbolg may be watching and won't appreciate your trying to sneak past. The dwarves in Thor Modan were thrilled to see Brann Bronzebeard, and were eager for news of their home. It seems they don't get that many travelers up there, particularly other dwarves. They're not there for socializing, though, and remain focused on their excavations. They have not yet discovered anything of note, but they're still hopeful. The Scourge forces at Drak'Tharon Keep are typical: nasty, violent, and focused. They hold the passes between [[Zul'Drak]], the [[Dragonblight]], and the rest of the Grizzly Hills, so that more Scourge forces can reach the east or return to [[Icecrown Glacier]]. ===Geography=== [[File:Grizzly Hills LoM.PNG|thumb|Map of Grizzly Hills in ''Lands of Mystery''.]] The Grizzly Hills are as hilly as the name suggests. Along the northern edges the land gains height and depth, approaching the level of small mountain ranges, while it flattens out a little in the south. Thick forest covers the land from end to end, broken only by small clearings or the space alongside one of the many streams and small rivers. Snow is everywhere but the region has little ice — the wind whistles overhead but the trees block it from entering down below, and the hills seem almost warm after the Dragonblight and the [[Borean Tundra]]. It's still dangerous, with treacherous slopes and hidden caves and partially frozen rivers, but better than most of the other regions. All manner of wild animals live here because the hills are full of life. [[Wolf|Wolves]], [[bear]]s, [[fox]]es, [[rabbit]]s and some small [[deer]] are the most common, though there are others as well. [[Mice]] and other rodents hide from the snowy [[owl]]s and other raptors in the trees, but mercifully [[snake]]s and [[spider]]s aren't present here, as they wouldn't be happy with the temperature. [[Wendigo]] and [[sasquatch]] prowl the hills, so it's best not to go out alone. The Drakkari live just north in Zul'Drak and sometimes their hunters drift down to the hills as well, in search of prey. The Grizzly Hills have three major settlements, each controlled by a different race. It's strange that all three can coexist here, and even stranger that they're all along the north edge. The southern hills have other furbolg tribes and the random trapper or traveler, but nothing larger than a small village. The Grizzly Hills surround Zul'Drak on both sides and reach all the way up to [[Crystalsong Forest]] and the [[Storm Peaks]], making it possible to travel between the northern and southern regions of Northrend without crossing the dangerous Drakkari territory.''[[Lands of Mystery]]'', pg. 111 ==Trivia== *Magical nuts called [[amberseed]]s can be harvested here. *The Grizzly Hills are based on {{Wp|redwood}} forests, an idea pitched by [[Gary Platner]].
